data.cultural_impact: The name Jagdish is associated with the Hindu deity Lord Vishnu, who is a major God in the Hindu pantheon and the preserver of the universe. The name is widely used among Hindu communities, particularly in North India, and is considered a powerful and auspicious name for both males and females.
data.spiritual_significance: Jagdish is believed to mean 'controller of the world' or 'regulator of the universe'. As a name of Lord Vishnu, it signifies the divine presence of the preserver and protector of the universe within an individual. It is a reminder of the ultimate spiritual truth that God is the ruler of all, and that one should strive to live a righteous and devotional life, following the teachings of Hinduism, in order to attain spiritual growth and ultimate liberation.

historical_references.reference: Jagdish was a common name for Hindu kings in the medieval period. One notable Jagdish was Jagdish Singh, the ruler of Jodhpur from 1581 to 1598. He is known for his military conquests and the expansion of the Jodhpur kingdom.

Another Jagdish was Jagadish Chandra Bose, a renowned Indian scientist who lived during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He is best known for his work in plant physiology and was one of the pioneers of radio science in India.
